levels.description: Before you dive into Data Science you need to know the basics of Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability, and Statistics. Do not get stuck trying to memorize every topic here, use this section as a reference point and return to it whenever a new topic uses math you do not know.

topics.title: Derivatives
topics.description: Fundamental concept of differential calculus representing rates of change, gradients, and optimization foundations. This topic is needed to understand how loss functions measure prediction error and how model parameters get updated during training.
author: Organic Chemistry Tutor
Khan Academy

topics.title: Matrix Multiplication
topics.description: Core linear algebra operation used for transforming feature vectors, linear projections, and neural network layers. This topic is needed to compute dense neural network layer outputs (W * X + b) and process batched dataset matrices efficiently on GPUs.
author: Organic Chemistry Tutor
Organic Chemistry Tutor

topics.title: Vectors & Vector Spaces
topics.description: Understanding vectors, dot products, vector norms (L1/L2), projections, and linear independence. This topic is needed to calculate similarity scores between text/image embeddings (cosine similarity) and apply L1/L2 regularization penalties to prevent model overfitting.
author: Dot Products, Organic Chemistry Tutor
L1, L2 norms
Projections, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Linear independence, Professor Dave Explains

topics.title: Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors
topics.description: Spectral decomposition methods essential for understanding Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and dimensionality reduction. This topic is needed to compress high-dimensional feature spaces down to their primary variance axes without losing core information.
author: Professor Dave Explains
3Blue1Brown

topics.title: Partial Derivatives & Gradients
topics.description: Multivariate calculus concepts required to understand gradient descent and loss function optimization. This topic is needed to compute backpropagation gradients across millions of weights simultaneously in deep neural networks.
author: Organic Chemistry Tutor
Organic Chemistry Tutor

topics.title: Probability Fundamentals & Bayes' Theorem
topics.description: Conditional probability, independence, joint distributions, and Bayesian inference core to machine learning models. This topic is needed to calculate confidence probabilities for classifications, run Naive Bayes baselines, and understand probabilistic modeling.
author: Conditional Probability, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Independent event, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Bayes Theorem, Organic Chemistry Tutor

topics.title: Descriptive & Inferential Statistics
topics.description: Mean, variance, standard deviation, distributions (Gaussian), hypothesis testing, p-values, and confidence intervals. This topic is needed to standardize feature scales (z-score normalization), evaluate model significance, and spot data leakage during EDA.
author: Mean, variance, and standard deviation, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Normal(Gaussian) distribution, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Hypothesis testing, Organic Chemistry Tutor
p-values, Organic Chemistry Tutor
Confidence intervals, Organic Chemistry Tutor

levels.description: Python's official documentation is the best source for learning the basics of this language.

These two sources below are enough for building a solid foundation in Classic Machine Learning. After completing them you can dive into the Deep Learning. In case you struggle finding a book in the internet or have troubles with coursera, below are the links to the videos with the explanations of Classic ML topics.

topics.title: Machine Learning Specialization
topics.description: Andrew Ng's "Machine Learning Specialization" course is the best starting point for learning classic ML. It is ideal for complete beginners because Andrew Ng explains most topics without advanced math, helping you build intuition for supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms. (Note: Coursera does not provide 100% financial aid anymore, but you can still audit the course for free without receiving a certificate.).
author: Andrew Ng

topics.title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
topics.description: After completing the Coursera course, you can read "Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow" by Aurélien Géron, which is considered an all-time classic among machine learning books. It provides the essential theory and math behind algorithms alongside hands-on practice with Scikit-Learn. For classic ML, you can focus on the first eight chapters.
author: Aurélien Géron

topics.title: Classification
topics.description: Binary and Multiclass Classification, and its evaluation metrics. Kaggle datasets to practice: MNIST, Titanic, Churn Prediction.
author: Binary & Metrics
Multiclass

topics.title: Regression
topics.description: Linear Regression, Gradient Descent, and Polynomial Regression. Kaggle dataset to train on: Price prediction.
author: Linear Regression
Gradient Descent
Polynomial Regression

topics.title: Decision Trees
topics.description: Tree-based algorithms and recursive splitting mechanics. Kaggle datasets to practice: MNIST, Titanic, Churn Prediction, Price prediction.
author: Decision Trees

topics.title: Ensemble Learning, Random Forests & Gradient Boosting
topics.description: Combining multiple weak learners using Ensemble techniques, Random Forests, and Gradient Boosting methods.
author: Ensemble & Random Forests
Gradient Boosting

topics.title: Unsupervised Learning Techniques
topics.description: Finding hidden patterns in unlabeled data using Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction, and Anomaly Detection.
author: Clustering
Dimensionality Reduction
Anomaly Detection

topics.title: Kaggle
topics.description: Creating personal projects is the best way to master the topics, Kaggle is the best source for finding the datasets for your projects.
author: Kaggle

levels.description: After mastering the Classic ML, you can dive into Deep Learning foundations.

topics.title: PyTorch Tutorials & Basics
topics.description: Before you start, it is recommended to check out these tutorials on PyTorch. It is the most popular tool in deep learning nowadays. You do not have to read both docs and watch the entire playlist, just choose what is the most comfortable for you.
author: PyTorch Official Docs
YouTube Playlist

topics.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
topics.description: After studying the basics of PyTorch, you can start reading Deep Learning with PyTorch (by Eli Stevens, Luca Antiga, and Thomas Viehmann). It is widely considered one of the best code-first introductions to both neural networks and PyTorch mechanics. Part 1 (Core PyTorch) contains everything you need to master core deep learning mechanics.
author: E.Stevens, L.Antiga, T.Viehmann

levels.description: Master specialized deep learning architectures across Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, and modern generative AI.

topics.title: Computer Vision (CV)
topics.description: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), object detection (YOLO), semantic segmentation, Vision Transformers (ViT), and feature backbones (DINOv2).
author: CS231n
PyTorch Docs

topics.title: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
topics.description: Text tokenization, embeddings (Word2Vec, SentenceTransformers), RNNs/LSTMs, Self-Attention mechanisms, and Transformer architectures (BERT, GPT).
author: Stanford CS224d
Hugging Face Docs

topics.title: Generative AI & LLM Systems
topics.description: Large Language Model fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector databases, and agentic workflows.
author: Hugging Face PEFT Docs
LangChain Docs
